_comment: AOS Sprint 23 — Engagement Templates. Delivery-kit annexes for the six domainTags that already have real, founder-authored proposal content in templates/proposals/ (DORA, EU AI Act, Security Governance, Third-Party Risk, GRC, Technology Risk), plus a general default for AI Deployment Governance (ADGL) when no more specific tag applies. Every discovery question, seed risk and reporting note below is a faithful paraphrase of that same real .md content — never a new, independently-invented regulatory claim. frameworkPriority is checked in order (mirrors service-catalogue.json's own domainTag-before-primaryService precedent) since an opportunity can carry more than one domainTag; the first match wins.

discoveryQuestions: Which ICT third parties are in scope for DORA resilience testing and monitoring?
What is the current incident reporting process, and does it meet DORA's notification timelines?
Is there a documented concentration-risk assessment across critical ICT third parties?

riskSeedRisks.why: DORA holds the regulated entity accountable for critical ICT third parties regardless of the vendor's own compliance status.
A vendor compliant at onboarding can drift out of alignment as the obligation itself evolves, with no commercial breach involved.

DORA.reportingNote: DORA expects an evidence trail that tracks the obligation itself, not just the contract — steering committee reporting should reflect ongoing ICT third-party monitoring status, not a one-time assessment.

discoveryQuestions: Which AI systems are in scope, and what risk tier does each fall into under the EU AI Act?
Is a conformity assessment required for any high-risk system, and on what timeline?
What technical documentation currently exists to support a conformity assessment?

riskSeedRisks.why: The Act's obligations vary by risk tier; an unclassified or misclassified system carries the wrong governance requirements.
A conformity assessment or notified body review requires documentation a working system rarely maintains by default.

EU AI Act.reportingNote: Reporting should track technical documentation and evidence-trail readiness per AI system risk tier, since that is what a conformity assessment will examine.

discoveryQuestions: Which standard or assessment is driving this work (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2, NIST CSF), and what does 'ready' mean for it?
Is control ownership assigned at the level where each control is actually operated?
Has a gap been discovered during a prior assessment rather than caught in advance?

riskSeedRisks.why: A control without an owner at the level it is actually operated is a gap an assessment will find.

riskSeedRisks.risk: Documented policy vs. operating practice gap
riskSeedRisks.why: A control can be documented as policy without reflecting how it is actually operated.

Security Governance.reportingNote: Reporting should track control gap remediation against the target baseline and assessment-readiness status.

discoveryQuestions: How are vendors segmented by criticality and data access today?
Who owns each vendor relationship after onboarding — through monitoring, renewal and exit?
What triggers a re-assessment when a vendor's subprocessors, data flows or controls change?

riskSeedRisks.why: The risk that materialises usually lives after signature, not at onboarding, and nothing triggers review unless someone is assigned to look for it.

riskSeedRisks.risk: Assessment not proportional to vendor criticality
riskSeedRisks.why: A single annual questionnaire for every vendor regardless of criticality misses where the real exposure sits.

Third-Party Risk.reportingNote: Reporting should track vendor monitoring cadence and re-assessment triggers proportional to criticality, not a single annual snapshot.

discoveryQuestions: Where has governance debt accumulated — duplicated committees, undocumented decisions, paper-only ownership?
Which governance decisions actually matter most, and are decision rights clear for each?
What would demonstrate this transformation is working, beyond a redesigned org chart?

riskSeedRisks.why: Duplicated committees, undocumented decisions and paper-only ownership accumulate faster than they get resolved.
A redesign that starts with reporting lines instead of decision rights usually reproduces the same ambiguity in a new structure.

GRC.reportingNote: Reporting should demonstrate value early through a governance effectiveness metric, not just a completed redesign.

discoveryQuestions: What are the specific risk decisions this function needs to make, and who currently makes them?
Does the current risk taxonomy and control library reflect actual exposure, or a template applied broadly?
Is assurance evidence produced ahead of audit, or reconstructed after the fact?

riskSeedRisks.why: A risk appetite statement engineering and business teams cannot apply in practice provides no real control.

riskSeedRisks.risk: Assurance evidence reconstructed after the fact
riskSeedRisks.why: Evidence produced only when an audit asks for it is a sign the assurance cycle isn't running continuously.

Technology Risk.reportingNote: Reporting should track whether assurance evidence is produced ahead of audit on an ongoing cycle, not reconstructed reactively.

discoveryQuestions: Is there a named owner for AI governance decisions today, or is this the first time one is being assigned?

riskSeedRisks.risk: No consistent risk evaluation across AI use cases
riskSeedRisks.why: Without one risk model calibrated to impact and reversibility, use cases get inconsistent scrutiny.

AI Deployment Governance (ADGL).reportingNote: Reporting should track whether governance decisions have a named owner and a documented approval gate — the core test of whether the operating model is actually in use.
